flags.label: Chain ends at undisclosed donors
flags.detail: 72% of COLOROFCHANGE PAC's receipts stop at organizations whose own funding is not on file (advocacy nonprofits, LLCs, trusts) rather than at named individuals, businesses or unions.

method: Backward walk over money edges only (Schedule A receipts from individuals and organizations, committee-to-committee transfers) into COLOROFCHANGE PAC, 3 hop(s) deep; independent expenditures are targeting edges and never appear. The walk starts from $3,270,351 of itemized 2023–2024 receipts as loaded from FEC bulk data (unitemized receipts, loans and offsets are not edges), and every expanded committee conserves dollars: its inbound edges sum to its receipts. Inbound edges under 1% of a committee's receipts are rolled into one 'other contributors' node, which counts as disclosed except for the organization dollars inside it. Each dollar takes the visibility of where the walk stopped: named individuals (including earmarks through ActBlue/WinRed, attributed to the person) are disclosed. Organizations that are not registered committees are classified from their name alone (no IRS lookup): a union or a business giving from its own treasury is disclosed — the named entity is the source; an LLC, trust, advocacy nonprofit (501(c)(4)-style names) or unclassifiable organization is dark, because whoever funds it is not on file with the FEC. 1 edge(s) point at a committee already expanded elsewhere in this chain and reuse its visibility mix instead of being walked twice. Visibility shares are preliminary; no 990 lookups were performed, so nothing is marked inferable.
